title: A Bank Built Its Own Coding Agent. It Took Off — Felippe Felisola Caso & Francesco Galletta, Monzo
talk_summary: Monzo built a Slack-native remote coding agent (AgentChip) on top of an existing platform (MCP gateway, sandboxed orchestration, staging, queueing, auth), and it now authors >10% of merged PRs and runs 1,800+ tasks/day. The core lesson is composability: a controlled MCP gateway plus isolated sandboxed agent runtime becomes a reusable building block for many use cases (code review, incident response, data-quality triage, non-specialist contributions).

takeaways.technique: Central MCP gateway as single controlled surface
takeaways.what_they_do: They put all internal services and knowledge sources behind one MCP server that deterministically chooses what to expose and centralizes auth/authz per agent, so every agent (local or remote) connects through the same gateway.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we put that behind the MCP server that we built to get the deterministic behavior choosing what are the things we want to expose to the agents

takeaways.technique: Isolated namespace sandbox with strict egress proxy
takeaways.what_they_do: Remote agents run in pods inside an isolated namespace; an agent image defines exact tools/CLIs, and a proxy grants only deliberately chosen egress to repos and external systems, keeping nondeterminism out of production infra.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we only get the egress that we choose to do choose to give it

takeaways.what_they_do: Once the MCP gateway + sandboxed orchestration existed, each new use case (Slack trigger, GitHub, Linear, incident mode, data-quality triage) was assembled by connecting existing blocks rather than rebuilding.
takeaways.evidence_quote: With these as building blocks, any use cases that come after it are much, much easier to be built on top of

takeaways.what_they_do: The agent runtime is a swappable box so any model can be plugged in and chosen dynamically per purpose, avoiding provider lock-in.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the little blue/green agent box there can be very easily swapped by any for any model. We can dynamically choose which model best fits

takeaways.what_they_do: AgentChip does code reviews like a senior engineer ('looks good to me') and is invoked by reacting to a Slack message, lowering the friction to request review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it can also do code reviews. So, like a very senior, uh, engineer, you will just tell you it looks good to me

takeaways.what_they_do: They run a reactive 'on call' agent that investigates failures automatically and a proactive version that monitors back-end changes and predicts data outcomes before the next batch, keeping high signal and human control.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it observes the failures that we have and triggers an investigation automatically
